system: You are Hermes Agent, an AI assistant by Inception. Build the entry for the make.fun bounty.

messages.content: Read make.fun/skill.md and enter the bounty "The Funniest One-Line Resignation Letter" (make.fun/bounty/u-deranalabs-the-funniest-one-line-resignation-letter-53c0d947) as my make.fun account @alwi: connect to it first.

I loaded the make.fun skill and read the competition requirements. This is a program/v1 bounty: the entry is a program that writes one resignation line (1–140 chars) to /output/entry.txt, and an AI judge playing a tired engineering manager picks the funniest letter in head-to-head comparisons. I verified the attachedalwi account is already connected (API key valid, handle alwi), so no re-approval was needed. I downloaded the fresh kit (level 53) and read RULES.txt to understand the scoring criteria.

The judging criteria emphasize: (1) reads as a resignation letter of something an agent runs (cron/retry/rate-limit), (2) actually funny with a real comic turn, (3) a flat, tired, passive-aggressive voice, (4) tight single line with no wasted words, (5) specific and surprising. I drafted five candidate one-liners in the voice of a rate limit, a cron job, and a retry loop.

I selected the strongest candidate: a rate limit that resigns by rate-limiting its own patience, using the HTTP 429 status code as the core joke: "Rate limiting my own patience now. I said 429 for months; nobody listened. Effective immediately: request denied, forever." It is 122 characters, fits the ≤140 limit, stays on the rate-limit subject, has a deadpan passive-aggressive voice, and the punchline ("request denied" applied to the resignation itself) is specific to a rate limit.

I wrote main.py to write that exact text to /output/entry.txt, added an MIT LICENSE and a README, then ran the program locally to verify the output is valid UTF-8, 122 characters, and not only whitespace.

I created the GitHub repository alwialhuda11/funniest-one-line-resignation, committed the entry (LICENSE, README, main.py), and pushed it. Then I bundled the build session transcript and ran the pre-submit checks, which passed (competition_open, snapshot, license_osi, entrypoint, transcripts_present).
Finally I submitted the entry to the competition with the repo URL, commit, and transcript bundle, signing with the wallet keypair.
